To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
extracellular ascorbate (vitamin C), a potent antioxidant, modulates phasically the excitability of striatal neurons in awake rats.
extracellular ascorbate (vitamin C), an antioxidant vitamin and neurotransmitter, modulates the activity of striatal neurons in a concentration-dependent manner.
ascorbate, an antioxidant vitamin, modulates glutamate-mediated activity in the rat striatum, and this effect may contribute to the behavioral effects of ascorbate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of asorbic acid (AA) in modulating striatally mediated behavior.
the role of extracellular ascorbate (vitamin C), an antioxidant vitamin that is released from neurons, in regulating striatal activity.
the effects of extracellular ascorbate on glutamatergic neurotransmission in the striatum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AA, an antioxidant vitamin, can act as a modulator of striatal activity, and the modulation of striatal activity by AA is a function of the dose, the time course, and the type of the antioxidant.
AA, apart of its antioxidant effects, has an excitatory effect in striatal neurons.
AA is a neuromodulator that can either facilitate or inhibit glutamate-induced excitation of striatal neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ascorbate is a neuromodulator of striatal function.
AA is an antioxidant that modulates phasic activity in the striatum.
AA is a neuromodulator that modulates the excitability of striatal neurons and that the effects of AA on striatal neurons are dependent upon the dose of AA applied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ascorbate is a neuromodulator of the glutamate system in the striatum.
AA is a modulator of striatal activity.
AA is a neuromodulator in the brain.
